# gslog Examples

This file shows each testable example of the gslog packages as a complete
program. `go test` runs each example that shows an output. Then it
compares the output of the example with the output below the program. Run
`make docs` to update this file.

## m4o.io/gslog

Package gslog contains the options, labels, and levels that the gslog handlers for Google Cloud Logging share.

The handlers are in the packages gcp and stdout.  This package and its dependencies import no module outside the standard library.  A program that uses only the stdout handler imports the packages gslog and stdout, and imports no client library.

### gslog

The options and the labels of this package apply to both handlers.  The example sets the default level of a stdout handler and adds a label from the context to a record.  The handler writes the record as one line of JSON.  A fixed time keeps the timestamp of the output the same on each run.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"time"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

func main() {
	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout, gslog.WithDefaultLeveler(slog.LevelDebug))

	ctx := context.Background()
	ctx = gslog.WithLabels(ctx, gslog.Label("tenant", "acme"))

	at := time.Date(2024, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, time.UTC)
	r := slog.NewRecord(at, slog.LevelDebug, "How now brown cow?", 0)
	r.AddAttrs(slog.String("animal", "cow"))

	_ = h.Handle(ctx, r)

}
```

Output:

```text
{"severity":"DEBUG","message":"How now brown cow?","timestamp":"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z","logging.googleapis.com/labels":{"tenant":"acme"},"animal":"cow"}
```

### gslog.WithLeveler

A program can change its log level while it runs, for example from an admin endpoint.  WithLeveler takes a slog.Leveler.  With a \*slog.LevelVar, the handler reads the variable for each record.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

func main() {
	var level slog.LevelVar
	level.Set(slog.LevelInfo)

	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout, gslog.WithLeveler(&level))

	ctx := context.Background()

	fmt.Println(h.Enabled(ctx, slog.LevelDebug))

	level.Set(slog.LevelDebug)

	fmt.Println(h.Enabled(ctx, slog.LevelDebug))

}
```

Output:

```text
false
true
```

### gslog.WithLogLevelFromEnvVar

A deployment sets the log level in an environment variable.  The program needs no change.  The value can be a level of Google Cloud Logging, such as "notice".  The case of the value is not important.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

func main() {
	const envVar = "FOO_LOG_LEVEL"
	_ = os.Setenv(envVar, "notice")
	defer func() {
		_ = os.Unsetenv(envVar)
	}()

	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout, gslog.WithLogLevelFromEnvVar(envVar))

	ctx := context.Background()

	fmt.Println(h.Enabled(ctx, slog.LevelInfo), h.Enabled(ctx, gslog.LevelNotice))

}
```

Output:

```text
false true
```

### gslog.WithDefaultLeveler

The program sets the default level for a deployment that does not set the environment variable.  A deployment that sets the variable overrides the default.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

func main() {
	const envVar = "FOO_LOG_LEVEL"
	_ = os.Unsetenv(envVar)

	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout,
		gslog.WithLogLevelFromEnvVar(envVar),
		gslog.WithDefaultLeveler(slog.LevelWarn),
	)

	ctx := context.Background()

	fmt.Println(h.Enabled(ctx, slog.LevelInfo), h.Enabled(ctx, slog.LevelWarn))

}
```

Output:

```text
false true
```

### gslog.WithSourceAdded

The Logs Explorer shows the file and the line of the log call when the entry has a source location.  The stdout handler writes the location in the field "logging.googleapis.com/sourceLocation".

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"path/filepath"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

func main() {
	var buf bytes.Buffer

	h := stdout.NewHandler(&buf, gslog.WithSourceAdded())
	logger := slog.New(h)

	logger.Info("How now brown cow?")

	// The timestamp is different on each run.  The line changes with each
	// edit of this file.  The example prints the name of the file and the
	// function.
	var line map[string]any

	_ = json.Unmarshal(buf.Bytes(), &line)

	loc, _ := line["logging.googleapis.com/sourceLocation"].(map[string]any)
	file, _ := loc["file"].(string)
	base := filepath.Base(file)

	fmt.Println(base, loc["function"])

}
```

Output:

```text
example_test.go m4o.io/gslog_test.ExampleWithSourceAdded
```

### gslog.WithReplaceAttr

A mapper keeps a secret out of the log.  The handler calls the mapper for each attribute, also for an attribute inside a group.  The first argument of the mapper holds the groups of the attribute, from the outer group to the inner group.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"time"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

// newRecord returns an Info record with a fixed time and the message "How
// now brown cow?".  A fixed time keeps the timestamp of the example output
// the same on each run.
func newRecord(attrs ...slog.Attr) slog.Record {
	at := time.Date(2024, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, time.UTC)

	r := slog.NewRecord(at, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?", 0)
	r.AddAttrs(attrs...)

	return r
}

// redactPassword is a gslog.AttrMapper that replaces the value of each
// attribute with the key "password".
func redactPassword(_ []string, a slog.Attr) slog.Attr {
	if a.Key == "password" {
		return slog.String(a.Key, "REDACTED")
	}

	return a
}

func main() {
	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout, gslog.WithReplaceAttr(redactPassword))

	auth := slog.Group("auth", slog.String("user", "jan"), slog.String("password", "hunter2"))
	r := newRecord(auth)

	_ = h.Handle(context.Background(), r)

}
```

Output:

```text
{"severity":"INFO","message":"How now brown cow?","timestamp":"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z","auth":{"user":"jan","password":"REDACTED"}}
```

### gslog.WithLabels

One call adds the labels of a tenant to the context.  A later call adds a label for one operation.  The entries of that operation have the labels of both calls.  The handler writes the labels in key order.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"time"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

// newRecord returns an Info record with a fixed time and the message "How
// now brown cow?".  A fixed time keeps the timestamp of the example output
// the same on each run.
func newRecord(attrs ...slog.Attr) slog.Record {
	at := time.Date(2024, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, time.UTC)

	r := slog.NewRecord(at, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?", 0)
	r.AddAttrs(attrs...)

	return r
}

func main() {
	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout)

	ctx := context.Background()
	ctx = gslog.WithLabels(ctx, gslog.Label("tenant", "acme"), gslog.Label("region", "eu"))
	ctx = gslog.WithLabels(ctx, gslog.Label("operation", "checkout"))

	_ = h.Handle(ctx, newRecord())

}
```

Output:

```text
{"severity":"INFO","message":"How now brown cow?","timestamp":"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z","logging.googleapis.com/labels":{"operation":"checkout","region":"eu","tenant":"acme"}}
```

## m4o.io/gslog/stdout

Package stdout contains a slog.Handler that writes each log record to a writer as one line of JSON.  The line has the structured logging format that the Google Cloud logging agent reads.

### stdout.NewHandler

NewHandler writes each entry to the writer as one line of JSON in the format that the Google Cloud logging agent reads.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"time"

	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

// newRecord returns an Info record with a fixed time and the message "How
// now brown cow?".  A fixed time keeps the timestamp of the example output
// the same on each run.
func newRecord(attrs ...slog.Attr) slog.Record {
	at := time.Date(2024, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, time.UTC)

	r := slog.NewRecord(at, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?", 0)
	r.AddAttrs(attrs...)

	return r
}

func main() {
	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout)

	r := newRecord(slog.String("animal", "cow"))

	_ = h.Handle(context.Background(), r)

}
```

Output:

```text
{"severity":"INFO","message":"How now brown cow?","timestamp":"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z","animal":"cow"}
```

### stdout.Handler.Handle (payloadMapping)

The stdout.Handler writes the nested group attributes of the handler as nested JSON objects.  The message is at the root of the object with the key "message".

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"time"

	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

// newRecord returns an Info record with a fixed time and the message "How
// now brown cow?".  A fixed time keeps the timestamp of the example output
// the same on each run.
func newRecord(attrs ...slog.Attr) slog.Record {
	at := time.Date(2024, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, time.UTC)

	r := slog.NewRecord(at, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?", 0)
	r.AddAttrs(attrs...)

	return r
}

type User struct {
	ID        string `json:"id"`
	FirstName string `json:"first_name"`
	LastName  string `json:"last_name"`
}

func main() {
	u := User{ID: "user-12234", FirstName: "Jan", LastName: "Doe"}

	var h slog.Handler = stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout)
	h = h.WithGroup("pub")
	h = h.WithAttrs([]slog.Attr{slog.Any("user", u)})

	_ = h.Handle(context.Background(), newRecord())

}
```

Output:

```text
{"severity":"INFO","message":"How now brown cow?","timestamp":"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z","pub":{"user":{"id":"user-12234","first_name":"Jan","last_name":"Doe"}}}
```

### stdout.NewHandler (withK8sPodinfo)

With the k8s.WithPodinfoLabels() option, stdout.Handler adds labels from the configured Kubernetes Downward API podinfo labels file to the field "logging.googleapis.com/labels".

The handler adds the prefix "k8s-pod/" to each label.  This follows the Google Cloud Logging conventions for Kubernetes Pod labels.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"time"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/k8s"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

// newRecord returns an Info record with a fixed time and the message "How
// now brown cow?".  A fixed time keeps the timestamp of the example output
// the same on each run.
func newRecord(attrs ...slog.Attr) slog.Record {
	at := time.Date(2024, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, time.UTC)

	r := slog.NewRecord(at, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?", 0)
	r.AddAttrs(attrs...)

	return r
}

func main() {
	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout, k8s.WithPodinfoLabels("../k8s/testdata/etc/podinfo"))

	ctx := context.Background()
	ctx = gslog.WithLabels(ctx, gslog.Label("a", "one"), gslog.Label("b", "two"))

	_ = h.Handle(ctx, newRecord())

}
```

Output:

```text
{"severity":"INFO","message":"How now brown cow?","timestamp":"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z","logging.googleapis.com/labels":{"a":"one","b":"two","k8s-pod/app":"hello-world","k8s-pod/environment":"stg","k8s-pod/tier":"backend","k8s-pod/track":"stable"}}
```

### stdout.NewHandler (withOpenTelemetryBaggage)

With the otel.WithBaggage() option, stdout.Handler adds the baggage.Baggage in the context as attributes.

The handler adds the prefix "otel-baggage/" to each baggage key.  The prefix makes collisions with other log attributes less likely.  The handler writes the baggage attributes after the attributes of the record.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"time"

	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage"

	"m4o.io/gslog/otel"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

// newRecord returns an Info record with a fixed time and the message "How
// now brown cow?".  A fixed time keeps the timestamp of the example output
// the same on each run.
func newRecord(attrs ...slog.Attr) slog.Record {
	at := time.Date(2024, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, time.UTC)

	r := slog.NewRecord(at, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?", 0)
	r.AddAttrs(attrs...)

	return r
}

func main() {
	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout, otel.WithBaggage())

	ctx := context.Background()
	ctx = baggage.ContextWithBaggage(ctx, otel.MustParse("a=one,b=two;p1;p2=val2"))

	_ = h.Handle(ctx, newRecord())

}
```

Output:

```text
{"severity":"INFO","message":"How now brown cow?","timestamp":"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z","otel-baggage/a":"one","otel-baggage/b":{"value":"two","properties":{"p1":null,"p2":"val2"}}}
```

### stdout.NewHandler (withOpenTelemetryTrace)

With the otel.WithTracing() option, stdout.Handler adds the OpenTelemetry trace.SpanContext information in the context to the tracing fields of the line.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"time"

	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"

	"m4o.io/gslog/otel"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

// newRecord returns an Info record with a fixed time and the message "How
// now brown cow?".  A fixed time keeps the timestamp of the example output
// the same on each run.
func newRecord(attrs ...slog.Attr) slog.Record {
	at := time.Date(2024, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, time.UTC)

	r := slog.NewRecord(at, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?", 0)
	r.AddAttrs(attrs...)

	return r
}

func main() {
	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout, otel.WithTracing("my-project"))

	traceID, _ := trace.TraceIDFromHex("52fc1643a9381fc674742bb0067101e7")
	spanID, _ := trace.SpanIDFromHex("d3e9e8c51cb190df")
	spanContext := trace.NewSpanContext(trace.SpanContextConfig{
		TraceID:    traceID,
		SpanID:     spanID,
		TraceFlags: trace.FlagsSampled,
	})

	ctx := trace.ContextWithSpanContext(context.Background(), spanContext)

	_ = h.Handle(ctx, newRecord())

}
```

Output:

```text
{"severity":"INFO","message":"How now brown cow?","timestamp":"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z","logging.googleapis.com/trace":"projects/my-project/traces/52fc1643a9381fc674742bb0067101e7","logging.googleapis.com/spanId":"d3e9e8c51cb190df","logging.googleapis.com/trace_sampled":true}
```

### stdout.NewHandler (withSourceAdded)

With the gslog.WithSourceAdded() option, stdout.Handler adds the field "logging.googleapis.com/sourceLocation" to the line.  This field is expensive to compute.

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"runtime"
	"time"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

func main() {
	var buf bytes.Buffer

	h := stdout.NewHandler(&buf, gslog.WithSourceAdded())

	var pcs [1]uintptr

	runtime.Callers(1, pcs[:])

	r := slog.NewRecord(time.Time{}, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?", pcs[0])

	_ = h.Handle(context.Background(), r)

	// The file is an absolute path.  The example prints the end of the path.
	var line map[string]any

	_ = json.Unmarshal(buf.Bytes(), &line)

	loc, _ := line["logging.googleapis.com/sourceLocation"].(map[string]any)
	file, _ := loc["file"].(string)
	loc["file"] = file[len(file)-len("stdout/example_test.go"):]

	b, _ := json.Marshal(loc)

	fmt.Println(string(b))

}
```

Output:

```text
{"file":"stdout/example_test.go","function":"m4o.io/gslog/stdout_test.ExampleNewHandler_withSourceAdded","line":"160"}
```

### stdout.NewHandler (withReplaceAttr)

With the gslog.WithReplaceAttr() option, stdout.Handler applies the supplied gslog.AttrMapper to each non-group attribute before the handler writes the attribute.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"time"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

// newRecord returns an Info record with a fixed time and the message "How
// now brown cow?".  A fixed time keeps the timestamp of the example output
// the same on each run.
func newRecord(attrs ...slog.Attr) slog.Record {
	at := time.Date(2024, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, time.UTC)

	r := slog.NewRecord(at, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?", 0)
	r.AddAttrs(attrs...)

	return r
}

// RemovePassword is a gslog.AttrMapper that elides password attributes.
func RemovePassword(_ []string, a slog.Attr) slog.Attr {
	if a.Key == "password" {
		return slog.Attr{}
	}

	return a
}

func main() {
	var h slog.Handler = stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout, gslog.WithReplaceAttr(RemovePassword))
	h = h.WithGroup("pub")
	h = h.WithAttrs([]slog.Attr{slog.String("username", "user-12234"), slog.String("password", "hunter2")})

	_ = h.Handle(context.Background(), newRecord())

}
```

Output:

```text
{"severity":"INFO","message":"How now brown cow?","timestamp":"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z","pub":{"username":"user-12234"}}
```

### stdout.NewHandler (withErrorReporting)

With the errorreporting.WithService() option, stdout.Handler writes the fields that Google Cloud Error Reporting reads.  The handler writes the fields in each record at level Error or higher.  The field "stack\_trace" holds the stack of the log call.

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"

	"m4o.io/gslog/errorreporting"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

func main() {
	var buf bytes.Buffer

	h := stdout.NewHandler(&buf, errorreporting.WithService("checkout", "v1.2.0"))
	l := slog.New(h)

	l.Error("Payment failed")

	// The stack trace is different on each run.  The example prints the
	// other fields.
	var line map[string]any

	_ = json.Unmarshal(buf.Bytes(), &line)

	report := map[string]any{
		"@type":          line["@type"],
		"serviceContext": line["serviceContext"],
	}

	b, _ := json.Marshal(report)

	fmt.Println(string(b))

}
```

Output:

```text
{"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.devtools.clouderrorreporting.v1beta1.ReportedErrorEvent","serviceContext":{"service":"checkout","version":"v1.2.0"}}
```

## m4o.io/gslog/gcp

Package gcp contains a slog.Handler that writes log records to Google Cloud Logging through the API client.

### gcp.WithHTTPRequest

With gcp.WithHTTPRequest, the gcp.Handler sets the HTTPRequest field of the logging.Entry.  The Logs Explorer shows the method, the status, the size, and the latency of the request in the summary of that entry.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"time"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"

	"m4o.io/gslog/gcp"
)

// statusRecorder is an http.ResponseWriter that records the status and the
// size of the response.
type statusRecorder struct {
	http.ResponseWriter

	status int
	size   int64
}

func (s *statusRecorder) WriteHeader(status int) {
	s.status = status

	s.ResponseWriter.WriteHeader(status)
}

func (s *statusRecorder) Write(b []byte) (int, error) {
	n, err := s.ResponseWriter.Write(b)
	s.size += int64(n)

	return n, err
}

// accessLog returns an HTTP handler that logs one record for each request.
// The HTTP handler gives the request, the status, the size, and the latency
// to the gcp.Handler in the context of the log call.
func accessLog(logger *slog.Logger, next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		start := time.Now()
		recorder := &statusRecorder{ResponseWriter: w, status: http.StatusOK, size: 0}

		next.ServeHTTP(recorder, r)

		request := &logging.HTTPRequest{
			Request:      r,
			Status:       recorder.status,
			ResponseSize: recorder.size,
			Latency:      time.Since(start),
		}
		ctx := gcp.WithHTTPRequest(r.Context(), request)

		logger.InfoContext(ctx, "Request completed")
	})
}

// PrintHTTPRequest is a gcp.Logger stub that prints the HTTPRequest field of
// the logging.Entry.  The latency is different on each run.  PrintHTTPRequest
// does not print the latency.
func PrintHTTPRequest(e logging.Entry) {
	r := e.HTTPRequest

	fmt.Printf("%s %s status=%d size=%d\n", r.Request.Method, r.Request.URL.Path, r.Status, r.ResponseSize)
}

// With gcp.WithHTTPRequest, the gcp.Handler sets the HTTPRequest field of the
// logging.Entry.  The Logs Explorer shows the method, the status, the size,
// and the latency of the request in the summary of that entry.
func main() {
	h := gcp.NewHandler(gcp.LoggerFunc(PrintHTTPRequest))
	logger := slog.New(h)

	app := http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte("created"))
	})
	server := accessLog(logger, app)

	request := httptest.NewRequestWithContext(context.Background(), http.MethodPost, "/orders", http.NoBody)

	server.ServeHTTP(httptest.NewRecorder(), request)

}
```

Output:

```text
POST /orders status=201 size=7
```

### gcp.NewHandler

The example creates a gcp.Handler with a GCP logging.Logger.  The handler maps each slog.Record to a logging.Entry.  The handler then passes the entry to the Log() method of its logging.Logger.  Flush sends the entries that the client still holds before the program exits.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log"
	"log/slog"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"

	"m4o.io/gslog/gcp"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	client, err := logging.NewClient(ctx, "my-project")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	lg := client.Logger("my-log")

	h := gcp.NewHandler(lg)
	l := slog.New(h)

	l.Info("How now brown cow?")

	err = lg.Flush()
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

### gcp.Handler.Handle (payloadMapping)

The gcp.Handler maps the slog.Record and the nested group attributes of the handler into a JSON object.  The message is at the root of the object with the key "message".

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"strconv"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson"

	spb "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"

	"m4o.io/gslog/gcp"
)

var (
	pw           = Password("pass-12334")
	pwObfuscated = slog.StringValue("<secret>")
	u            = &User{
		ID:        "user-12234",
		FirstName: "Jan",
		LastName:  "Doe",
		Email:     "jan@example.com",
		Password:  pw,
		Age:       32,
		Height:    5.91,
		Engineer:  true,
	}
)

type Manager struct{}

// Password is a type that implements fmt.Stringer, json.Marshaler, and
// slog.LogValuer.  Each implementation returns an obfuscated value.
type Password string

func (p Password) String() string {
	return "<secret>"
}

func (p Password) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
	return []byte(strconv.Quote("<secret>")), nil
}

func (p Password) LogValue() slog.Value {
	return pwObfuscated
}

type User struct {
	ID        string   `json:"id"`
	FirstName string   `json:"first_name"`
	LastName  string   `json:"last_name"`
	Email     string   `json:"email"`
	Password  Password `json:"password"`
	Age       uint8    `json:"age"`
	Height    float32  `json:"height"`
	Engineer  bool     `json:"engineer"`
	Manager   *Manager `json:"manager"`
}

// PrintJsonPayload is a gcp.Logger stub that prints the logging.Entry
// Payload field as a JSON string.
func PrintJsonPayload(e logging.Entry) {
	b, _ := protojson.Marshal(e.Payload.(*spb.Struct))

	var j map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(b, &j)
	b, _ = json.Marshal(j)
	fmt.Println(string(b))
}

func main() {
	h := gcp.NewHandler(gcp.LoggerFunc(PrintJsonPayload))
	l := slog.New(h)
	l = l.WithGroup("pub")
	l = l.With(slog.Any("user", u))

	l.Info("How now brown cow?")

}
```

Output:

```text
{"message":"How now brown cow?","pub":{"user":{"age":32,"email":"jan@example.com","engineer":true,"first_name":"Jan","height":5.91,"id":"user-12234","last_name":"Doe","manager":null,"password":"\u003csecret\u003e"}}}
```

### gcp.Handler.Handle (withLabels)

The gcp.Handler adds the labels in the context to the Labels field of the logging.Entry.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"sort"
	"strings"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/gcp"
)

// PrintLabels is a gcp.Logger stub that prints the logging.Entry's
// Labels field.
func PrintLabels(e logging.Entry) {
	keys := make([]string, 0)
	for k := range e.Labels {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	sort.Strings(keys)

	var sb strings.Builder
	for _, k := range keys {
		if sb.Len() > 0 {
			sb.WriteString(", ")
		}
		sb.WriteString(k + "=" + e.Labels[k])
	}

	fmt.Println(sb.String())
}

func main() {
	h := gcp.NewHandler(gcp.LoggerFunc(PrintLabels))
	l := slog.New(h)

	ctx := context.Background()
	ctx = gslog.WithLabels(ctx, gslog.Label("a", "one"), gslog.Label("b", "two"))

	l.Log(ctx, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?")

}
```

Output:

```text
a=one, b=two
```

### gcp.NewHandler (withK8sPodinfo)

With the k8s.WithPodinfoLabels() option, gcp.Handler adds labels from the configured Kubernetes Downward API podinfo labels file to the Labels field of the logging.Entry.

The handler adds the prefix "k8s-pod/" to each label.  This follows the Google Cloud Logging conventions for Kubernetes Pod labels.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"sort"
	"strings"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/gcp"
	"m4o.io/gslog/k8s"
)

// PrintLabels is a gcp.Logger stub that prints the logging.Entry's
// Labels field.
func PrintLabels(e logging.Entry) {
	keys := make([]string, 0)
	for k := range e.Labels {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	sort.Strings(keys)

	var sb strings.Builder
	for _, k := range keys {
		if sb.Len() > 0 {
			sb.WriteString(", ")
		}
		sb.WriteString(k + "=" + e.Labels[k])
	}

	fmt.Println(sb.String())
}

func main() {
	h := gcp.NewHandler(gcp.LoggerFunc(PrintLabels), k8s.WithPodinfoLabels("../k8s/testdata/etc/podinfo"))
	l := slog.New(h)

	ctx := context.Background()
	ctx = gslog.WithLabels(ctx, gslog.Label("a", "one"), gslog.Label("b", "two"))

	l.Log(ctx, gslog.LevelCritical, "Danger, Will Robinson!")

}
```

Output:

```text
a=one, b=two, k8s-pod/app=hello-world, k8s-pod/environment=stg, k8s-pod/tier=backend, k8s-pod/track=stable
```

### gcp.NewHandler (withOpenTelemetryBaggage)

With the otel.WithBaggage() option, gcp.Handler adds the baggage.Baggage in the context as attributes.

The handler adds the prefix "otel-baggage/" to each baggage key.  The prefix makes collisions with other log attributes less likely.  A baggage attribute has precedence over an attribute that already has the same key.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"
	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson"

	spb "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"

	"m4o.io/gslog/gcp"
	"m4o.io/gslog/otel"
)

// PrintJsonPayload is a gcp.Logger stub that prints the logging.Entry
// Payload field as a JSON string.
func PrintJsonPayload(e logging.Entry) {
	b, _ := protojson.Marshal(e.Payload.(*spb.Struct))

	var j map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(b, &j)
	b, _ = json.Marshal(j)
	fmt.Println(string(b))
}

func main() {
	h := gcp.NewHandler(gcp.LoggerFunc(PrintJsonPayload), otel.WithBaggage())
	l := slog.New(h)

	ctx := context.Background()
	ctx = baggage.ContextWithBaggage(ctx, otel.MustParse("a=one,b=two;p1;p2=val2"))

	l.Log(ctx, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?")

}
```

Output:

```text
{"message":"How now brown cow?","otel-baggage/a":"one","otel-baggage/b":{"properties":{"p1":null,"p2":"val2"},"value":"two"}}
```

### gcp.NewHandler (withOpenTelemetryTrace)

With the otel.WithTracing() option, gcp.Handler adds the OpenTelemetry trace.SpanContext information in the context to the tracing fields of the logging.Entry.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"strings"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"
	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"

	"m4o.io/gslog/gcp"
	"m4o.io/gslog/otel"
)

// PrintTracing is a gcp.Logger stub that prints the logging.Entry's
// tracing fields.
func PrintTracing(e logging.Entry) {
	var sb strings.Builder

	sb.WriteString("trace: ")
	sb.WriteString(e.Trace)
	sb.WriteString(" span: ")
	sb.WriteString(e.SpanID)
	sb.WriteString(" flags: ")
	if e.TraceSampled {
		sb.WriteString("01")
	} else {
		sb.WriteString("00")
	}

	fmt.Println(sb.String())
}

func main() {
	h := gcp.NewHandler(gcp.LoggerFunc(PrintTracing), otel.WithTracing("my-project"))
	l := slog.New(h)

	traceId, _ := trace.TraceIDFromHex("52fc1643a9381fc674742bb0067101e7")
	spanId, _ := trace.SpanIDFromHex("d3e9e8c51cb190df")

	ctx := context.Background()
	ctx = trace.ContextWithRemoteSpanContext(ctx, trace.NewSpanContext(trace.SpanContextConfig{
		TraceID:    traceId,
		SpanID:     spanId,
		TraceFlags: trace.FlagsSampled,
	}))

	l.Log(ctx, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?")

}
```

Output:

```text
trace: projects/my-project/traces/52fc1643a9381fc674742bb0067101e7 span: d3e9e8c51cb190df flags: 01
```

### gcp.NewHandler (withSourceAdded)

With the gslog.WithSourceAdded() option, gcp.Handler adds the SourceLocation field to the logging.Entry.  This field is expensive to compute.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson"

)

// PrintSourceLocation is a gcp.Logger stub that prints the logging.Entry's
// SourceLocation field.
func PrintSourceLocation(e logging.Entry) {
	sl := e.SourceLocation
	sl.File = sl.File[len(sl.File)-len("gcp/example_test.go"):]

	b, _ := protojson.Marshal(sl)

	var j map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(b, &j)
	b, _ = json.Marshal(j)
	fmt.Println(string(b))
}

func main() {
	h := gcp.NewHandler(gcp.LoggerFunc(PrintSourceLocation), gslog.WithSourceAdded())
	l := slog.New(h)

	l.Log(context.Background(), slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?")

}
```

Output:

```text
{"file":"gcp/example_test.go","function":"m4o.io/gslog/gcp_test.ExampleNewHandler_withSourceAdded","line":"267"}
```

### gcp.NewHandler (withReplaceAttr)

With the gslog.WithReplaceAttr() option, gcp.Handler applies the supplied gslog.AttrMapper to each non-group attribute before the handler logs the attribute.

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"strconv"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson"

	spb "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"

	"m4o.io/gslog"
	"m4o.io/gslog/gcp"
)

var (
	pw           = Password("pass-12334")
	pwObfuscated = slog.StringValue("<secret>")
)

type Manager struct{}

// Password is a type that implements fmt.Stringer, json.Marshaler, and
// slog.LogValuer.  Each implementation returns an obfuscated value.
type Password string

func (p Password) String() string {
	return "<secret>"
}

func (p Password) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
	return []byte(strconv.Quote("<secret>")), nil
}

func (p Password) LogValue() slog.Value {
	return pwObfuscated
}

type User struct {
	ID        string   `json:"id"`
	FirstName string   `json:"first_name"`
	LastName  string   `json:"last_name"`
	Email     string   `json:"email"`
	Password  Password `json:"password"`
	Age       uint8    `json:"age"`
	Height    float32  `json:"height"`
	Engineer  bool     `json:"engineer"`
	Manager   *Manager `json:"manager"`
}

// PrintJsonPayload is a gcp.Logger stub that prints the logging.Entry
// Payload field as a JSON string.
func PrintJsonPayload(e logging.Entry) {
	b, _ := protojson.Marshal(e.Payload.(*spb.Struct))

	var j map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(b, &j)
	b, _ = json.Marshal(j)
	fmt.Println(string(b))
}

// RemovePassword is a gslog.AttrMapper that elides password attributes.
func RemovePassword(_ []string, a slog.Attr) slog.Attr {
	if a.Key == "password" {
		return slog.Attr{}
	}
	return a
}

func main() {
	h := gcp.NewHandler(gcp.LoggerFunc(PrintJsonPayload), gslog.WithReplaceAttr(RemovePassword))
	l := slog.New(h)
	l = l.WithGroup("pub")
	l = l.With(slog.String("username", "user-12234"), slog.String("password", string(pw)))

	l.Info("How now brown cow?")

}
```

Output:

```text
{"message":"How now brown cow?","pub":{"username":"user-12234"}}
```

### gcp.NewHandler (withLogLevelFromEnvVar)

With the gslog.WithLogLevelFromEnvVar() option, gcp.Handler reads its log level from the environment variable that the key names.

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson"

	spb "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"

	"m4o.io/gslog/gcp"
)

// PrintJsonPayload is a gcp.Logger stub that prints the logging.Entry
// Payload field as a JSON string.
func PrintJsonPayload(e logging.Entry) {
	b, _ := protojson.Marshal(e.Payload.(*spb.Struct))

	var j map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(b, &j)
	b, _ = json.Marshal(j)
	fmt.Println(string(b))
}

func main() {
	const envVar = "FOO_LOG_LEVEL"
	_ = os.Setenv(envVar, "ERROR")
	defer func() {
		_ = os.Unsetenv(envVar)
	}()

	h := gcp.NewHandler(gcp.LoggerFunc(PrintJsonPayload), gslog.WithLogLevelFromEnvVar(envVar))
	l := slog.New(h)

	l.Info("How now brown cow?")
	l.Error("The rain in Spain lies mainly on the plane.")

}
```

Output:

```text
{"message":"The rain in Spain lies mainly on the plane."}
```

### gcp.NewHandler (withErrorReporting)

With the errorreporting.WithService() option, gcp.Handler writes the fields that Google Cloud Error Reporting reads.  The handler writes the fields in the payload of each record at level Error or higher.  The field "stack\_trace" holds the stack of the log call.

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"

	spb "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"

	"m4o.io/gslog/errorreporting"
	"m4o.io/gslog/gcp"
)

// PrintErrorReport is a gcp.Logger stub that prints the fields "@type" and
// "serviceContext" of the logging.Entry Payload.  The stack trace is
// different on each run.
func PrintErrorReport(e logging.Entry) {
	payload := e.Payload.(*spb.Struct).AsMap()

	report := map[string]any{
		"@type":          payload["@type"],
		"serviceContext": payload["serviceContext"],
	}

	b, _ := json.Marshal(report)

	fmt.Println(string(b))
}

func main() {
	h := gcp.NewHandler(gcp.LoggerFunc(PrintErrorReport), errorreporting.WithService("checkout", "v1.2.0"))
	l := slog.New(h)

	l.Error("Payment failed")

}
```

Output:

```text
{"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.devtools.clouderrorreporting.v1beta1.ReportedErrorEvent","serviceContext":{"service":"checkout","version":"v1.2.0"}}
```

### gcp.LoggerFunc

A test receives the entries of the handler with LoggerFunc in place of a logging.Logger.  The example prints the severity and the message of each entry.

```go
package main

func main() {
```

### gcp.Handler.WithLeveler

One component of a program can log at a lower level than the rest.  The copy from WithLeveler shares the logger of the handler, so the entries of both go to the same log.

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"

	"cloud.google.com/go/logging"

// PrintJsonPayload is a gcp.Logger stub that prints the logging.Entry
// Payload field as a JSON string.
func PrintJsonPayload(e logging.Entry) {
	b, _ := protojson.Marshal(e.Payload.(*spb.Struct))

	var j map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(b, &j)
	b, _ = json.Marshal(j)
	fmt.Println(string(b))
}

func main() {
	h := gcp.NewHandler(gcp.LoggerFunc(PrintJsonPayload), gslog.WithLeveler(slog.LevelInfo))
	verbose := h.WithLeveler(slog.LevelDebug)

	checkout := slog.New(h)
	payments := slog.New(verbose)

	payments.Debug("Card authorized")

}
```

```text
{"message":"Card authorized"}
```

## m4o.io/gslog/otel

Package otel contains options that include OpenTelemetry baggage and tracing in logging records.

The options are in a separate package.  Because of this, a module that does not need OpenTelemetry tracing has fewer dependencies.

### otel.WithTracing (httpServer)

A program with no OpenTelemetry SDK can link its logs to the trace of each request.  The HTTP handler from withTraceContext puts the span context of the traceparent header in the context of the request.  The log call gives that context to the slog handler.

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"

	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation"

	"m4o.io/gslog/otel"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

// withTraceContext returns an HTTP handler that reads the W3C traceparent
// header of each request.  The HTTP handler puts the span context of the
// header in the context of the request.  A program that uses otelhttp with
// a configured propagator does not need this HTTP handler.
func withTraceContext(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	propagator := propagation.TraceContext{}

	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		carrier := propagation.HeaderCarrier(r.Header)
		ctx := propagator.Extract(r.Context(), carrier)
		r = r.WithContext(ctx)

		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}

func main() {
	var buf bytes.Buffer

	h := stdout.NewHandler(&buf, otel.WithTracing("my-project"))
	logger := slog.New(h)

	app := http.HandlerFunc(func(_ http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		logger.InfoContext(r.Context(), "Order placed")
	})
	server := withTraceContext(app)

	request := httptest.NewRequestWithContext(context.Background(), http.MethodGet, "/orders", http.NoBody)
	request.Header.Set("traceparent", "00-52fc1643a9381fc674742bb0067101e7-d3e9e8c51cb190df-01")

	server.ServeHTTP(httptest.NewRecorder(), request)

	// The timestamp is different on each run.  The example prints the
	// tracing fields.
	var line map[string]any

	_ = json.Unmarshal(buf.Bytes(), &line)

	tracing := map[string]any{
		"logging.googleapis.com/trace":         line["logging.googleapis.com/trace"],
		"logging.googleapis.com/spanId":        line["logging.googleapis.com/spanId"],
		"logging.googleapis.com/trace_sampled": line["logging.googleapis.com/trace_sampled"],
	}

	b, _ := json.Marshal(tracing)

	fmt.Println(string(b))

}
```

Output:

```text
{"logging.googleapis.com/spanId":"d3e9e8c51cb190df","logging.googleapis.com/trace":"projects/my-project/traces/52fc1643a9381fc674742bb0067101e7","logging.googleapis.com/trace_sampled":true}
```

### otel.WithBaggage (httpServer)

An upstream service sends the tenant and the user of a request in the baggage header.  The HTTP handler from withBaggage puts the baggage in the context of the request, and each log entry of the request gets the members as attributes.

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"

	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation"

	"m4o.io/gslog/otel"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

// withBaggage returns an HTTP handler that reads the W3C baggage header of
// each request.  The HTTP handler puts the baggage of the header in the
// context of the request.  A program that uses otelhttp with a configured
// propagator does not need this HTTP handler.
func withBaggage(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	propagator := propagation.Baggage{}

	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		carrier := propagation.HeaderCarrier(r.Header)
		ctx := propagator.Extract(r.Context(), carrier)
		r = r.WithContext(ctx)

		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}

func main() {
	var buf bytes.Buffer

	h := stdout.NewHandler(&buf, otel.WithBaggage())
	logger := slog.New(h)

	app := http.HandlerFunc(func(_ http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		logger.InfoContext(r.Context(), "Order placed")
	})
	server := withBaggage(app)

	request := httptest.NewRequestWithContext(context.Background(), http.MethodGet, "/orders", http.NoBody)
	request.Header.Set("baggage", "tenant=acme,user=jan;role=admin")

	server.ServeHTTP(httptest.NewRecorder(), request)

	// The timestamp is different on each run.  The example prints the
	// baggage attributes.
	var line map[string]any

	_ = json.Unmarshal(buf.Bytes(), &line)

	attrs := map[string]any{
		"otel-baggage/tenant": line["otel-baggage/tenant"],
		"otel-baggage/user":   line["otel-baggage/user"],
	}

	b, _ := json.Marshal(attrs)

	fmt.Println(string(b))

}
```

Output:

```text
{"otel-baggage/tenant":"acme","otel-baggage/user":{"properties":{"role":"admin"},"value":"jan"}}
```

### otel.MustParse

A job with no incoming request sets the baggage in the context itself. MustParse builds the baggage from a literal that always parses.  A fixed time keeps the timestamp of the output the same on each run.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"time"

	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/baggage"

	"m4o.io/gslog/otel"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

func main() {
	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout, otel.WithBaggage())

	bag := otel.MustParse("tenant=acme,job=nightly-report")
	ctx := baggage.ContextWithBaggage(context.Background(), bag)

	at := time.Date(2024, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, time.UTC)
	r := slog.NewRecord(at, slog.LevelInfo, "Report started", 0)

	_ = h.Handle(ctx, r)

}
```

Output:

```text
{"severity":"INFO","message":"Report started","timestamp":"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z","otel-baggage/job":"nightly-report","otel-baggage/tenant":"acme"}
```

## m4o.io/gslog/otel/detect

Package detect contains an option that includes OpenTelemetry tracing with a project ID from the environment of the process.

### detect.WithTracing

A service on Google Cloud gets its project ID from the metadata server. The program then needs no configuration for the trace prefix.  Off Google Cloud, the environment variable GOOGLE\_CLOUD\_PROJECT gives the project ID. The example has no output, because the project ID depends on the environment of the process.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"

	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"

	"m4o.io/gslog/otel/detect"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

func main() {
	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout, detect.WithTracing())
	logger := slog.New(h)

	traceID, _ := trace.TraceIDFromHex("52fc1643a9381fc674742bb0067101e7")
	spanID, _ := trace.SpanIDFromHex("d3e9e8c51cb190df")
	spanContext := trace.NewSpanContext(trace.SpanContextConfig{
		TraceID:    traceID,
		SpanID:     spanID,
		TraceFlags: trace.FlagsSampled,
	})

	ctx := trace.ContextWithSpanContext(context.Background(), spanContext)

	logger.InfoContext(ctx, "How now brown cow?")
}
```

## m4o.io/gslog/k8s

Package k8s contains options that include labels from the Kubernetes Downward API podinfo labels file in logging records.

The options are in a separate package.  Because of this, a module that does not need labels from the Kubernetes Downward API has fewer dependencies.

### k8s.WithPodinfoLabels

In a Pod, a volume of the Downward API holds the labels file.  The option takes the directory of the volume.  Each entry then has the labels of the Pod.  The example uses the labels file in the testdata directory.  The handler adds the prefix "k8s-pod/" to each label.  The handler writes the labels in key order.  A fixed time keeps the timestamp of the output the same on each run.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"time"

	"m4o.io/gslog/k8s"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

func main() {
	h := stdout.NewHandler(os.Stdout, k8s.WithPodinfoLabels("testdata/etc/podinfo"))

	at := time.Date(2024, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, time.UTC)
	r := slog.NewRecord(at, slog.LevelInfo, "How now brown cow?", 0)

	_ = h.Handle(context.Background(), r)

}
```

Output:

```text
{"severity":"INFO","message":"How now brown cow?","timestamp":"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z","logging.googleapis.com/labels":{"k8s-pod/app":"hello-world","k8s-pod/environment":"stg","k8s-pod/tier":"backend","k8s-pod/track":"stable"}}
```

## m4o.io/gslog/errorreporting

Package errorreporting contains an option for Google Cloud Error Reporting. The option causes the handler to write the fields that Error Reporting reads.  The handler writes the fields in each record at level Error or higher.  The package imports no module outside the standard library.

### errorreporting.WithService

Error Reporting reads an entry that has the fields of a ReportedErrorEvent. The handler writes these fields in each record at level Error or higher. The Info record has no report fields.  The Error record has the type, the service context, and a stack trace.

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"strings"

	"m4o.io/gslog/errorreporting"
	"m4o.io/gslog/stdout"
)

func main() {
	var buf bytes.Buffer

	h := stdout.NewHandler(&buf, errorreporting.WithService("checkout", "v1.2.0"))
	logger := slog.New(h)

	logger.Info("Payment started")
	logger.Error("Payment failed")

	// The timestamp and the stack trace are different on each run.  The
	// example removes these two fields and prints the rest of each line.
	for line := range strings.Lines(buf.String()) {
		var fields map[string]any

		_ = json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &fields)

		delete(fields, "timestamp")
		delete(fields, "stack_trace")

		b, _ := json.Marshal(fields)

		fmt.Println(string(b))
	}

}
```

Output:

```text
{"message":"Payment started","severity":"INFO"}
{"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.devtools.clouderrorreporting.v1beta1.ReportedErrorEvent","message":"Payment failed","serviceContext":{"service":"checkout","version":"v1.2.0"},"severity":"ERROR"}
```
